narrative:
The model determined that you have a 56% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeds the approval threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the loan amount you requested, and the duration of the loan. Your checking account status was the most important reason for the denial. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants (only 12.6% of them show this status), and it pushed the prediction noticeably toward bad credit risk. The amount you asked for worked in your favor: at 2,600 DM it was below the average requested by approved applicants (about 3,020 DM), which helped pull the prediction toward approval. The 18-month duration was also slightly helpful, as it sits just below the average length seen among those who were approved.

Taken together, the negative signal from your checking account outweighed the positive effects of the smaller loan size and shorter term, leading to the rejection.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account—bringing it into positive territory or building a buffer—before reapplying. This single change is likely to have the biggest impact on future decisions. Consider speaking with a loan officer about steps you can take to strengthen your profile.
